messages:
sam: Heads-up 50: marketing needs a cold-vs-warm cache decay sweep + per-token tail latency CSVs for the quantized launch collateral. Targets: 13B q4_0 and 70B q8_0. Deliverables: raw CSVs, per-seq heatmap PNG, short methodology blurb, and a one-paragraph safe-claim sentence for PR. Deadline next Tue EOD. Can runtime take this?

nina: We can run it. A couple clarifying q's: what do you mean by cache decay sweep? Do you want artificially long prefix reuse windows, or sequentially increasing idle times between requests? Also streaming vs non-streaming?

sam: Good q. Two parts: 1) prefix-reuse: run with identical prompt repeated to exercise KV cache (reused prefix) for 1, 10, 100 token prefixes. 2) idle decay: run same payload after varying idle intervals: 0s (warm), 30s, 300s, 1800s. Include both parts for 13B; for 70B do only the idle decay. Streaming: include streaming for 13B tests.

raj: Noted. We'll capture per-request fields: request_id, seq_length, prefix_tokens, idle_seconds, model_variant, node_type, first_token_ms, last_token_ms, tokens_generated, gpu_util_pct, compile_time_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate. We'll also log worker_pids and docker_image for reproducibility.

sam: For seq lengths use 64, 256, 1024. Concurrency sweep: 1, 6, 12. Warmup policy: 20s warmup, 60s steady for each point. Use marketing payload `mkting-cache-2026-03-21` and deterministic sampling.

nina: Scheduling note: some quant backends (pg_quant) may JIT/compile on first use; we'll mark compile_time_ms and exclude those outliers from steady-state aggregates but keep them in raw CSV. Also kernel selection may differ across node images; we'll include kernel_version column.

sam: Great. Marketing also wants a simple "safe claim" draft we can use that doesn't overstate anything. Something like: "Observed X ms median p50 improvement at 13B quantized in steady-state (streaming) compared to baseline non-streaming on equivalent hardware. See artifact for full distribution and methodology." Please flag any comparisons that are not apples-to-apples.

raj: Will include a comparisons table showing exact hardware/node, batch, seq, and streaming flags. We'll also generate a PNG heatmap (latency in ms) with x-axis concurrency, y-axis idle_seconds, separate panels per seq_length, and small inset showing p99.

bench-bot: Job submitted: cache-decay-2075550001-01 queued by nina for Tue 06:00 UTC. ETA artifacts Wed 14:00 UTC. Artifact prefix: s3://redwood-marketing/cache-decay-2075550001/

nina: Repro config snippet we'll store with runs:
````
models: [redwood-13b-q4_0, redwood-70b-q8_0]
seq_lengths: [64,256,1024]
concurrency: [1,6,12]
warmup_seconds: 20
steady_seconds: 60
prefix_sizes: [1,10,100]
idle_seconds: [0,30,300,1800]
streaming: [true,false]
payload_set: mkting-cache-2026-03-21
random_seed: 2026
metrics: [per_request_ms,p50,p95,p99,first_token_ms,tokens_per_sec,kv_cache_hit_rate,compile_time_ms]
artifact_bucket: s3://redwood-marketing/cache-decay-2075550001/
````

raj: We'll also attach a README with exact CLI commands, the payload SHA256, and a short troubleshooting section listing known variance sources (compile jitter, host kernel mismatches, transient network).

sam: Perfect 50: please also add a small note in the README that marketing must not compare streaming steady-state numbers to cold-start compile numbers. If there's any live variance >30% on p95, call it out and flag for re-run.

ops-scheduler: Scheduled: cache-decay-2075550001-01 will reserve A100 nodes at Tue 06:00 UTC. H100 spot attempt scheduled after baseline if capacity available.

nina: Will ping here when artifacts land and include the safe-claim draft for legal review. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
